title: Fifth unvaccinated person dies of measles; CDC still not counting all deaths
gist: Pennsylvania reported a fifth measles death in a Lancaster County-centered outbreak of 943 cases across 39 counties (119 in the past week, 176+ hospitalized). US cases hit at least 3,659 this year, the most since 1991, yet the CDC under RFK Jr. has altered its death-counting criteria and reports only two deaths.

insights.claim: Pennsylvania's measles outbreak, which began in late April with Lancaster County as epicenter, has reached 943 cases across 39 counties, including 119 in the last seven days, with at least 176 hospitalized.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: An accelerating outbreak raises local healthcare utilization and public health spending.
insights.quote: The updated case count as of Wednesday is 943 across 39 counties, including 119 cases reported in just the last seven days.

insights.claim: The five Pennsylvania deaths are the state's first measles deaths in 35 years and the only US measles deaths reported this year; victims include two infants too young to vaccinate, an unvaccinated 18-year-old and an unvaccinated 40-year-old with COPD.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Mortality is recurring after decades of absence, signaling a structural public health deterioration.
insights.quote: Prior to these five deaths in Pennsylvania, the state had not reported a measles death in 35 years.

insights.claim: Pennsylvania state nurses have administered more than 8,500 MMR doses this year, including over 5,500 at pop-up clinics in outbreak areas; the two-dose MMR vaccine provides 97% lifetime protection.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Outbreaks drive reactive vaccine demand at the state level.

insights.claim: The CDC has tallied at least 3,659 US measles cases this year, more than last year and the highest on record since 1991, after measles was declared eliminated in 2000.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
entities: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
insights.so_what: The US risks losing measles elimination status, a reputational and public health cost.
insights.quote: a tally higher than last year’s and the highest on record since 1991
insights.locator: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

insights.claim: Under Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s influence, the CDC altered its criteria for counting measles deaths and reports only two deaths despite five in Pennsylvania.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
entities: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
insights.so_what: Politicized federal health data reduces reliability of official statistics for policy and market decisions.
insights.quote: the CDC has resisted reporting the deaths in Pennsylvania, instead altering the criteria for what it counts as a measles death.
insights.locator: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

insights.claim: The author attributes measles' resurgence to anti-vaccine misinformation, including from Kennedy, driving continuously slipping vaccination rates and all-time-high exemptions.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Declining vaccine uptake is a headwind for vaccine makers and a rising public health cost.
insights.quote: vaccination exemptions have hit an all-time high, and the highly infectious virus has come roaring back.

insights.claim: In 2025 the US had three measles deaths tied to a West Texas outbreak, the first since 2015.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Two consecutive years of deaths confirm a trend rather than a one-off.
